text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- U.S. FUNDS WANT TO BUY BANESPA

Government sources say the federal government is talking to a group of Brazilian investors who are interested in buying Sao Paulo state bank Banespa and who are associates of American David Bonderman in the private equity fund Newbridge Latin America.
-- BANCO DO BRASIL TO ISSUE UP TO $500 MLN ABROAD
Banco do Brasil is planning to issue 10-year eurobonds worth between $400 million and $500 million with the aim to finance Brazilian companies.
-- NEW TAPE LINKS SERGIO MOTTA TO CASH-FOR-VOTES SCANDAL

New taped telephone conversations link Communications Minister Sergio Motta to a scandal in which five deputies were allegedly paid off to vote for a bill allowing President Cardoso to stand for re-election.
-- PRISONERS HOLD 23 HOSTAGES IN TWO STATES
A total of 23 people were taken hostage in three prison riots in Sao Paulo and Santa Catarina states.
-- CONFLICT BETWEEN U.S. AND BRAZIL CREATES FTAA IMPASSE

A U.S.-Brazilian war of words in which both sides accuse each other of protectionist trade policies is threatening to hamper this weeks talks in Belo Horizonte on creating a Free Trade Area of the Americas by 2005.
-- NEW AUTOPSY BACKS UP CLAIM DESIGNER WAS MURDERED
A new autopsy backs up claims that the death of fashion designer Zuzu Angel in April 1976, one of the most controversial cases during Brazil's military dictatorship, was not an accident but murder.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
